newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs firmer as stocks weak, rate fears almost over.
newsitem.headline: JGBs firmer as stocks weak, rate fears almost over.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Wednesday's morning session firmer as Tokyo stocks were weighed down by the yen's recent rise against the dollar.

Some traders said market sentiment had turned bullish since Tuesday as concerns that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) could raise interest rates in July had subsided given the yen's rise and since there was no U.S. rate change at Tuesday's Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
But others said they would wait for the results of the day's 10-year JGB auction.
The key June contract was up 0.21 at 124.71 at midday after opening at 124.70. It moved between 124.62 and 124.91 in turnover of 32,421 contracts.
Earlier, the Finance Ministry offered one trillion worth of 2.7 percent 10-year JGBs via an auction. The terms were in line with market expectations, traders said.

"A good auction result may further boost JGBs," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. "Those who expected an early rise in interest rates and sold since mid-April corrected their views, and this resulted in an improvement in sentiment," he said.
The dealer said a view had spread in the market that the BOJ will not be able to raise interest rates unless the dollar firms and stabilises at the upper end of 110-120 yen.
Continued rolling forward of short positions to the September contract ahead of a benchmark shift provided support for the June, traders said.

"I don't know if sentiment has changed or not," said a dealer at a "Big Four" brokerage house. "Buying emerged in futures, but the cash market was quiet ahead of the auction." The yield of key 182nd 10-year JGB was down 0.035, at 2.435 percent, at noon.
The results of the auction are due at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT).
On Wednesday, Japan's largest grouping of labour unions said it would call on the Bank of Japan to raise the official discount rate but a third dealer this had had little impact.
"We are not paying too much attention to comments outside of the BOJ. We need to focus more on figures to sound out strength of the economic recovery."
